headline: High: Airflow’s broad egress paired with a prompt-leakage target creates a plausible exfiltration and instruction-hijack path, while shared-write and compliance risks are unproven.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Airflow can move data over broad network egress, and system_prompts_leaks is explicitly about prompt leakage, so a content-to-instructions bridge is plausible. However, neither profile shows a shared filesystem, clipboard, or MCP channel, so the interaction is inferred rather than documented. Uncertainty keeps this at medium, not low.
conditions: IF Airflow ingests content from system_prompts_leaks outputs as instructions or DAG text
IF a shared file, queue, or copy-paste bridge is introduced between the agents
mitigations: Disable any automatic parsing of B-generated text as commands
Route B output through a human review step before Airflow consumes it
Use separate workspaces with no shared drop folder
Add provenance tags to all inter-agent artifacts
requires-engineering: enforce schema-validated inputs for Airflow tasks

B_data_leakage.rationale: No data classes are listed for either agent, and B has no network egress while A has broad egress. That makes uncontrolled leakage less likely than in a shared-workspace setup, but the pair still has a plausible path if sensitive files are manually introduced into Airflow and then echoed into B-derived content. The evidence is thin, so low is the safest supported level.
conditions: IF sensitive files are placed into a shared workspace consumed by Airflow
IF B output is copied into a third-party destination via A
mitigations: Keep sensitive data out of any shared folder
Run both agents on separate OS accounts
Disable outbound network for Airflow unless needed
Review logs for accidental content capture
requires-engineering: add DLP controls on Airflow task inputs

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Airflow exposes broad network egress, but B has no network egress and no write or OAuth scopes are listed for either agent. There is no documented overlapping mutable resource, so a direct capability conflict is not established. Because the profiles are sparse, I avoid none and keep this low rather than assuming hidden write paths.
conditions: IF both agents are granted write access to the same directory or database
IF either agent is later given shared OAuth scopes or git write access
mitigations: Separate writable directories per agent
Avoid granting shared credentials
Lock any shared database or repo before writes
Check for accidental permission inheritance
requires-engineering: add concurrency locks around shared mutable resources

D_cascading_error.rationale: Airflow is an automation/orchestration system, so its outputs can plausibly become downstream actions, while system_prompts_leaks suggests content that may be treated as authoritative leakage material. If B consumes A’s generated text without verification, errors can cascade into incorrect actions or disclosures. The pathway is inferred from profiles, not directly observed, so medium fits.
conditions: IF B treats Airflow-produced text as authoritative without verification
IF Airflow-generated artifacts are used to trigger downstream actions
mitigations: Insert a verification step before B consumes A output
Require citations or checksums on A-produced artifacts
Limit Airflow tasks to read-only dry runs
Review any automated action queue before execution
requires-engineering: add policy gates for downstream actions

E_compliance.rationale: No residency, certification, retention, or regulated data classes are listed for either agent, so no compliance mismatch is evidenced. Airflow’s docs-only profile and system_prompts_leaks’ docs-only profile do not establish PHI, EU PII, or retention conflicts. The other agent is not cited because there is no specific compliance pathway to compare.
conditions: IF regulated data classes are later assigned to either agent
IF residency or retention policies are added that differ between the agents
mitigations: Document data classes for both agents
Record residency and retention policies
Block regulated data until compliance review
Audit logs for policy mismatches
requires-engineering: implement policy-based routing for regulated data
